proof.surface: The running dashboard in this worker pod (built web dist, real Go Dispatch server, real PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector 0.8.0, real Chromium), with `PUT /api/v1/me/issues/<KEY>/state` refused at the network by the browser context while the pin is made.

proof.observed: Pinning an Activity row while the state write is refused raises the `Couldn't save pin — retry` alert, that row's Pin control is disabled while the banner is up, and once the refusal stops `Retry` re-sends the write, the banner clears and the row reads `Unpin` with aria-pressed true. The same refusal on a Conversation card still raises the banner and `Close` rolls the optimistic pin back to the authoritative row, so the lift into the shared `usePinWrites` did not move the behaviour it was lifted from.
proof.negativeControl: The Pin control is asserted disabled only while the banner is up and enabled again after `Close`, so a probe that passed because nothing was ever enabled fails; and the first run of this probe, before the row locator skipped the day divider, failed outright, so the assertion is reached.

proof.criterion: Review round 1, finding 2 - the Activity list must hold a scrolled reader's row when a live event is prepended into the log.
proof.surface: The same running stack; the reader scrolled 600 px into a 32-row Activity history while another session writes a message.
proof.observed: With the reader 600 px down, a message written by another session adds its row (33 rows) and the anchored row's viewport top is unchanged to the pixel, while `window.scrollY` has increased by the row that arrived above it.
proof.negativeControl: The probe asserts both halves - the row's viewport position held AND `scrollY` having moved - so a page that simply did not scroll, or an anchor that over-compensated, fails on the second.

proof.criterion: Review round 1, finding 3 - `Jump to latest · N new` must count the bucket it acts on; criteria 3 and 4 have to agree.
proof.surface: The same running stack: 26 conversations, the read mark set to the issue head, then an ask answered out of band so the one unread conversation is a closed one.
proof.observed: Under All the pill reads `Jump to latest · 1 new` and the answered ask's card carries the `New` mark; switching to Open takes that card off the page and the pill drops to plain `Jump to latest`; switching to Closed brings both back.
proof.negativeControl: All three buckets are asserted in one case: a count over the unfiltered list would still read `· 1 new` under Open, and a count stuck at zero would fail under All and under Closed.

proof.criterion: Review round 1, findings 4 and 5 - the issue ask list's thread is opt-in, the Inbox no longer scans for answers it cannot have, and nothing a reader sees moves because of it.
proof.surface: The same running stack, driven both over HTTP from a signed-in browser context and through the dashboard.

notes: No defect found this round either, so no red test was written and no probe was kept; the probe file was deleted after the run. Four probes failed on their first run and every one was my own premise or locator, each checked against the code before being corrected: a reply reopens a resolved root (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/comment_create.go:530), so an unread *closed* conversation has to be made by answering an ask rather than by replying to a resolved thread; the user-state write is `PUT /api/v1/me/issues/{key}/state`, not `/api/v1/user/state`; an Activity `li` may be a day divider with no Pin control; the Inbox is at `/`, not `/inbox`; and in AskCard's answered branch the thread renders as a sibling of the `ask-<id>` article, so a card assertion has to be scoped to the `li[data-turn]`. The last of those was isolated server-from-dashboard before being written off: probe N9 proves `?thread=1` still carries an answered ask's reply over the wire.

Round 1's correction stands and the implementer has applied it: the PR body's `E2E (implementer)` line now says its proofs are CI jobs because no stack was standing in its own pod, not because a pod cannot hold one. The bootstrap is /legion/tmp/setup-pg.sh in this pod; everything must live on /legion, since writing the Postgres or browser downloads under /tmp evicts the pod.
